page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor, utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, with no simultaneous multithreading. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

This instance includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed, low-latency local block storage directly attached to the host. For network connectivity, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48,571.1 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,706.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.31 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached operations at 1894.03 GB/sec, but drops to 173.34 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. Database operations perform at an average tier, with Passmark database operations scoring 20,441.91 and Redis SET operations reaching 40.61 million operations per second.

The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. However, the lower single-core performance and weak memory score represent a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks. This instance is best suited for multi-threaded compute-intensive workloads, local database hosting, static web serving, software compilation, and containerized microservices that benefit from local NVMe storage.
